The objectives of implementing integrated services for women and children empowerment are:
a. To guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of women and children in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

c. To encourage the community to carry out its obligations in the prevention and protection of women and children in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

g. To encourage the provision of facilities, infrastructure and various types of services in various areas of life for women and children such as data and information centers, counseling, psychological and medical therapy, assistance, education and training, referral centers, skills training and so on as an effort to improve the quality of life of women, welfare and protection of children managed by the community independently.

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 41
(1) In order to provide protection services to women and children who are victims of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A.

b. community elements; and
c. academic elements.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

All forms of violence in general and acts of violence against women and or children are a form of human rights violation and constitute a form of crime against human dignity as well as discriminatory treatment, therefore it is the obligation of the Government and Regional Government to realize the guarantee of security/protection of honor, dignity, property, freedom from torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and discriminatory treatment.

Current developments show that acts of violence against women and or children still frequently occur within the family environment as well as within society which clearly result in suffering and hardship for women and or children physically, psychologically, or sexually including threats of certain actions, coercion, or deprivation of rights.

Services and handling, guidance as well as empowerment of women and or children have not been optimal so far. Various causes mentioned above are that most women and or children victims of acts of violence choose to remain silent and their problems end with women and children falling into powerlessness.

This regional regulation is intended as an effort by the Lamandau Regency Government to meet the demands of society by providing services for the rights of women and children victims of acts of violence in a comprehensive, clear and firm manner to protect or side with victims.

Article 42
(1) The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) facilitates the provision of various services for the community, both physical and non-physical, which include information, referral, consultation/counseling, skills training and other activities.
(2) The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) can also serve as a place to conduct training for cadres who have great commitment and concern for women's and children's issues in all fields (health, education, economy, politics, law as well as protection of women and children from acts of violence and human trafficking) so that they can then work together and participate in providing services to the community in a forum for improving the quality of life and protection for women and children.

Article 30
Upon application by the victim or their representative, the court may consider to:
a. Establish a special condition;
b. Modify or revoke a special condition of the protection order.

5.1.rationale: The Indonesian text does provide for collaboration with non-government actors. Pasal 1(10) defines prevention as efforts by “lembaga pemerintah maupun non pemerintah” (government and non-government institutions). Pasal 1(11) on protection includes “lembaga sosial atau lembaga kemasyarakatan lainnya” (social institutions/other community institutions). Pasal 41(2) makes P2TP2A membership include “unsur masyarakat” (community elements), and Pasal 22(d) requires integrated coordination with “lembaga sosial yang dibutuhkan korban.” These passages were present in the retrieved English candidates (e.g., Art. 1 definitions; Art. 22; Art. 41). The judge was too strict in requiring the literal term “NGO/civil society organisation” and overlooked that the regulation explicitly includes non-government institutions/community/social institutions as partners, so this is primarily an evaluation failure rather than missing retrieval.

10. Prevention is all efforts carried out by government or non-government institutions aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children.
11. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, advocates, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against children and women.

14. Misery is any act that results in or may result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.

22. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of service facility for women and children in an effort to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, politics, law, protection and prevention of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children.

Article 42
(1) The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) facilitates the provision of various services for the community, both physical and non-physical, which include information, referral, consultation/counseling, skills training and other activities.
(2) The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) can also serve as a place to conduct training for cadres who have great commitment and concern for women's and children's issues in all fields (health, education, economy, politics, law as well as protection of women and children from acts of violence and human trafficking) so that they can then work together and participate in providing services to the community in a forum for improving the quality of life and protection for women and children.

5.4.rationale: The Indonesian text does engage the education sector: Pasal 13(5) states children in and around schools must be protected from violence by teachers/school administrators/peers and other educational institutions (“lembaga pendidikan lainnya”). Also, P2TP2A membership includes “unsur akademisi” (Pasal 41(2)(c)), and Pasal 42(2) discusses training cadres concerned with issues including “pendidikan.” The retrieved English passages include these points, and the judge’s ‘Yes’ is consistent with the Indonesian source. Thus the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.

Article 15
The Government and other state institutions are obligated and responsible to provide special protection to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances (napza) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.

Article 30
Upon application by the victim or their representative, the court may consider to:
a. Establish a special condition;
b. Modify or revoke a special condition of the protection order.

Article 43
Programs that can be implemented by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) include: a. Women's empowerment.
b. Protection of women and children from acts of violence and human trafficking.
c. Communication, information and education.
d. Increasing community member participation.
e. Increasing management capacity.

Article 3
The objectives of implementing integrated services for women and children empowerment are:
a. To guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of women and children in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
b. To prevent and protect women and children from violence.
c. To encourage the community to carry out its obligations in the prevention and protection of women and children in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
d. To rehabilitate victims as a result of violence experienced.
e. To take action against perpetrators of domestic violence.
f. To provide sex-disaggregated data and information on issues of empowerment and protection of women and children for the community that needs it.
g. To encourage the provision of facilities, infrastructure and various types of services in various areas of life for women and children such as data and information centers, counseling, psychological and medical therapy, assistance, education and training, referral centers, skills training and so on as an effort to improve the quality of life of women, welfare and protection of children managed by the community independently.

CHAPTER IV
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR CHILDREN AND VICTIMS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE

Article 34
(1) The Police may arrest and subsequently detain without a warrant any perpetrator believed to have violated a protection order, even though the violation was not committed at the place where the police officer is assigned.
(2) The arrest and detention as referred to in paragraph (1), must be provided with an arrest and detention warrant after 1x24 (one times twenty-four) hours.
(3) Suspension of detention does not apply to detention as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2).

CHAPTER VI
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 41
(1) In order to provide protection services to women and children who are victims of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A.
(2) The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in (1), consists of: a. regional government elements;
b. community elements; and
c. academic elements.
(3) The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

6.5.rationale: The Indonesian regulation explicitly addresses disability in multiple places: Pasal 4(h) provides rights for “anak yang menyandang cacat” to obtain special education; Pasal 4(k) states “Setiap anak yang menyandang cacat berhak memperoleh rehabilitasi, bantuan sosial, dan pemeliharaan taraf kesejahteraan sosial”; Pasal 13(4) ensures equal opportunity/accessibility for children with physical/mental disabilities; and Pasal 15 includes “anak yang menyandang cacat” among groups entitled to special protection. These were reflected in the retrieved English candidates (Art. 4, 13, 15). The judge’s ‘Yes’ is supported by the Indonesian text, so the golden label ‘No’ appears wrong.
